title: The Broke Researcher's Survival Manual: Zero-Cost Strategies to Fund Your PhD, Defend Your
description: It is 2 a.m. You are staring at a bank balance that will not cover the application fee, the rent, and the bursar's bill — all due in the same week. You have sent three honest emails asking what to do, and every reply has been silence, a bounce-back, or a polite sentence that answers nothing. Here is the truth no welcome packet ever prints: the fee waivers, the funding loopholes, the grievance routes, and the legal exit doors all exist. They are official. They are free. And they are buried in PDFs and renamed offices because the system runs more smoothly when low-income and first-generation students never find them. The Broke Researcher's Survival Manual is the map to the cracks. This is a no-fluff, copy-and-paste field guide for first-generation, low-income, working-class, and early-career researchers across the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and the EU. Every method is 100% legal and rated for success rate, time cost, and risk. Every email comes in three tones — Polite Standard, Firm Assertive, and Humble Appeal — with a line-by-line fill guide and follow-up scripts for 24 and 48 hours of silence. Inside you get: Ten emergency fixes with three-move action plans you can run today: fee waivers, blocked graduations, rejection seasons, visa cliffs, eviction, financial collapse, misconduct blame, failed qualifying exams, missing paychecks, and mental-health crises. The funding-first strategy that can take an application season from $1,000+ down to $0, plus the waiver routes that turn an open-access bill into nothing. Toxic-advisor defense: documentation systems universities cannot ignore, escalation ladders, and the realistic advisor switch. title: Burnout Broke My Body: A Capacity-Based System to Catch Burnout Before Your Body Does
description: Your calendar looks survivable. Something underneath it isn't. You're the one people count on, at work and at home. From the outside it looks handled. But your focus, your sleep, and your body keep wearing down. Often the body notices first. Capacity is what you actually have. Load is what you're carrying. When Load exceeds Capacity, that's Bad Math . Right-Sizing changes the plan until it fits. Maria Vought, a nurse turned operations leader, ran capacity math for a living until her own ran out. Her story opens the book. The rest is a system you can use the same week: small changes, no wellness lectures, and no giving up your ambitions. Inside: The Daily Capacity Snapshot: a two-minute check on whether today fits The STOP Check: four questions that turn a quick yes into a better one The Pressure Map and Access Map: find what's driving the strain, and decide what gets access to you The Reduced-Capacity Plan: built on a better day, before you need it If this sounds like someone you love, it was written for them too. And it's for anyone who keeps saying "after this season." You are not the problem. title: An American Problem: How the Country Built--and the Supreme Court Broke--the Voting Rights
description: The rise and fall of the Voting Rights Act, from the triumph of its passage in 1965 to its evisceration by the Supreme Court in their 2013 decision in Shelby County v. Holder The Voting Rights Act of 1965 finally made good on the promise of the Fifteenth Amendment, which nearly a century before had granted Black Americans the right to vote. The Voting Rights Act was the crowning achievement of the Civil Rights Movement, which had battled for years against voting laws that made it all but impossible for Black Americans to cast a ballot. The act was a resounding success, bringing Americans of all races and ethnicities into the democratic process. And then, in 2013, the Supreme Court brought this progress to a screeching halt with their decision in Shelby County v. Holder . In this book, Michael Miller and Kevin Morris offer a sweeping history of the Voting Rights Act and the attacks it has suffered. Miller and Morris explain that central to the act's success was its requirement that states and localities with a history of discrimination get federal permission to change their voting rules—a novel approach known as "preclearance." It was this requirement that the Shelby County decision eviscerated. Miller and Morris trace the devastating effect of Shelby County , using advanced research techniques to prove that the decision unleashed racially discriminatory voting policies. The result is a nation in which Americans of color cast fewer ballots, and in which the ballots they do cast count for less. But the story does not end there: the Supreme Court continues to undermine what remains of the Voting Rights Act. What President Lyndon B. Johnson called "an American problem," formerly kept in check by a strong federal law, once again threatens voting rights.  ©2026 Princeton Univ

description: Broke must be rough, dominant, and confident. Stepping into his new role as MC Vice President, the mask he wears screams "Don't screw with me!" but that just hides the part he can't show. Inside this sweet, shy man are insecurities stemming from trauma he encountered as a teenager that still haunt him. Roan is as sweet as they come. The epitome of pure; good, honest and innocent. Thrown into danger by her job, she's attacked by a member of the Russian mob. Left lying helpless in the hospital, one phone call binds her to the rough, handsome biker who would do anything to protect her. With danger lurking she has no other option but to hide beneath his wings. Both hide behind themselves, yet are determined to force the other to become the person they truly are. Will they each overcome their inner battles as well as the threat from the Russian mob who leaves a trail of bodies in its wake? Will Broke be able to save Roan's life or let his own slip through his fingers? Each book in the Broken Deeds MC series is a complete standalone story featuring a new couple.
